title: The Last Person Who Remembers: A Novel
tagline: She can hear a lie in any recording. She cannot hear one in her own past.
author: Prince Bhalse
synopsis: Mira Sen is a forensic audio analyst. She has spent her career separating real voices from fabricated ones. Then a routine custody case brings her the voice of her dead brother.

Her mother insists Mira was an only child. An authenticated hospital record says Arin Sen existed. A childhood wardmate remembers Mira as a girl who frightened other children. And a recording made before Mira ever heard of the case contains her own voice: If he comes back, don't let him tell you which one of us survived.

As Mira searches for the brother she remembers, she discovers that everyone who knew her has a different account of their shared past — and that she once underwent a procedure designed to rebuild her identity.

The evidence is real. The memories are sincere. The stories cannot all be true. The closer Mira comes to the truth, the less certain she becomes that the woman investigating Arin's disappearance is the same woman who lived it.
Some people are forgotten. Others are remembered wrong. Mira Sen is about to learn which is worse.
pitch: A gripping psychological suspense novel following a forensic audio analyst who discovers the voice of her dead brother — only to find every record and memory of her past beginning to fracture.

title: The Liar's Game
series: The Elara Voss Investigations — Book One
tagline: The room is the womb and the tomb
author: Prince Bhalse
synopsis: Around her, the world was on fire with a graduate's worth of goodbyes. On the banister, Mira Chen left behind everything that would have made her recognizable: her denim jacket, a black notebook, and a key she was never supposed to find. Elara Voss walked away from the party, crossed the campus lawn, and opened that key's door to find something the university had been keeping beneath its oldest library for a hundred years.
A room that official blueprints say does not exist.
A ledger of a secret society whispering through every board, every department, every murder disguised as accident for a century.
A list of dead men with Elara's name already at the bottom.

There is only one way out of a hundred-year secret: prove the account, destroy the room, and make the society's own history undo them. But the deeper Elara descends, the harsher the truth becomes: the room was not hidden from her. It was waiting for her. And the last entry in the ledger already knows her name.
pitch: A whip-smart, candlelit thriller about secret societies, hidden rooms, and the women who read the world for what is missing.
